decisions.context: Every transaction must receive its score before authorization, so predictions must be computed during the request. The scoring path also needs capacity for peak traffic.

alternatives.label: Online computation serving
cons: Availability: each request depends on live serving capacity

alternatives.label: Scheduled batch prediction deployment
pros: Availability: scores large sets on a schedule
cons: Latency: cannot score each transaction before authorization

decisions.rationale: The authorization deadline makes request-time scoring decisive; scheduled batch scoring cannot meet it. This gives up the decoupling batch processing offers and requires the online path to remain available.
consequences: Keep prediction computation on the authorization path.
Live serving capacity must be available when transactions arrive.

decisions.context: The payments authorization flow needs to submit transaction features and receive a fraud score synchronously. The interface must fit within the brief’s short response window.

alternatives.label: REST prediction microservice
pros: Availability: separates and independently deploys prediction service
cons: Latency: service and network calls add overhead

alternatives.label: gRPC model interface
cons: Availability: requires compatible clients and service setup

decisions.rationale: The synchronous authorization flow makes a direct API request the clearest fit, and REST prediction microservices are described in “Architecting a Machine Learning Pipeline: How to build scalable Machine Learning systems - Part 2/2.” We accept network-call overhead to keep the model independently deployable.
consequences: Authorization depends on the prediction service response.
The API contract must carry transaction inputs and return a score.

decisions.context: Scoring needs features available within tens of milliseconds, while later audits require the feature values associated with a score to remain available. Serving and durable storage must support both needs.

alternatives.label: Online/offline feature-store architecture
pros: Latency: online store supports fast inference reads
cons: Availability: requires keeping complementary stores aligned

alternatives.label: Online feature-serving pipeline
pros: Latency: materializes features for online inference
cons: Auditability: durable feature history is not explicit

alternatives.label: Central analytical ML data platform
cons: Latency: analytical storage may not serve tight online reads

decisions.rationale: The latency deadline and need to retain features both decide this choice: complementary online and durable stores address the two access patterns. We accept the operational cost of keeping the stores aligned; “MLOps: Continuous delivery and automation pipelines in machine learning” and “MLOps: What It Is, Why it Matters, and How To Implement It (from a Data Scientist Perspective)” describe this architecture.
consequences: Maintain online and durable feature representations.
Record the feature values used for each scored transaction.

decisions.context: Auditors need to identify the model version and features behind each score. This requires linking deployed artifacts and datasets to the model lifecycle metadata.

alternatives.label: Comprehensive ML lifecycle traceability
pros: Auditability: links artifacts, runs, metadata, and datasets
cons: Availability: requires lifecycle metadata capture and governance

alternatives.label: Artifact version control
cons: Auditability: does not alone link features and scores

alternatives.label: Data-to-model lineage management
pros: Auditability: connects dataset versions to model metadata
cons: Auditability: does not alone establish per-score feature values

decisions.rationale: The requirement to identify both the model version and features decides in favor of lifecycle-wide traceability over artifact-only versioning. We accept broader metadata and governance work; “Continuous Intelligence: Moving Machine Learning Application into Production Reliably” and “MLOps Principles” describe integrated lifecycle tracking.
consequences: Capture model, run, dataset, and deployment metadata.
Associate score records with the deployed model version and feature snapshot.

decisions.context: Transaction scoring must keep working through peaks without allowing model computation to miss its short deadline. Serving capacity therefore needs to respond to changing demand.

alternatives.label: Elastic resource scaling
cons: Availability: scaling may lag sudden demand changes

alternatives.label: Scale-to-zero serving
cons: Latency: startup delay risks the scoring deadline
Availability: no warm capacity at low demand

decisions.rationale: Peak availability decides the choice: elastic scaling can add capacity with demand, while scale-to-zero risks startup delay against the latency deadline. We accept some unused warm capacity; “Productionizing Machine Learning with a Microservices Architecture” discusses scaling resources with workload demand.
consequences: Set scaling limits and observe peak resource use.
Keep sufficient warm capacity to protect the response deadline.

uncovered: Per-score audit record format, retention period, and access controls.
Fraud-specific fallback behavior when features or model serving are unavailable.
